facts.title: Myth as private horror
facts.body: Goya’s Saturn Devouring His Son, one of the Black Paintings from his Quinta del Sordo house, remakes the Cronus myth as raw panic on a dark wall.

facts.title: A god without majesty
facts.body: Saturn is gaunt, naked, and frantic — divinity stripped to appetite and fear.

facts.title: A child already half-gone
facts.body: The pale body hangs limp in his grip — time devouring what it fears will replace it.

facts.title: Eyes that cannot look away
facts.body: Saturn’s bulging eyes stare past us — terror mid-bite.

facts.title: Fingers like claws
facts.body: Hands dig into flesh with desperate force — not ceremony, but hunger.

facts.title: No room, no sky
facts.body: The background is near-black emptiness — myth without a stage.

facts.title: Paint as wound
facts.body: Reds and raw flesh tones flare against the dark — the mural’s violence made intimate.
